issues.body: `onSelectClass` changes `selection` before validating the new IRI, but increments `instanceRef` only after `instanceListQuery` succeeds. If a safe class request is in flight and the user next selects a class with an IRI rejected by `instanceListQuery`, the old request retains the current ticket and may later overwrite the rejection error with its rows. Those rows are then rendered under `Instances of <new class>`, silently attributing instances to the wrong class.
issues.fix_hint: Allocate/increment the instance request ticket immediately on entry to `onSelectClass`, before building or validating the query, so every new selection invalidates prior work. Add a focused interleaving test: start request A, select an unsafe class B, resolve A, and assert B retains its rejection error and never displays A's rows.
issues.title: Rejected class selection does not cancel the previous drill-down request

verdict.summary: The stable-revision publication race fixed in round 3 remains resolved, but round 4 still has a separate drill-down race: selecting a class whose IRI cannot safely be embedded returns before invalidating the prior instance request. A previously started request can then resolve and publish rows beneath the newly selected, rejected class, contradicting the panel's claim that drill-down results belong to the selected bubble. The focused tests cover IRI rejection and request cancellation independently, but not this real interleaving.
